claim: GABAergic interneurons can be subdivided into three subclasses: parvalbumin positive (PV), somatostatin positive (SOM) and serotonin positive neurons.
source: GABAergic interneurons can be subdivided into three subclasses: parvalbumin positive (PV), somatostatin positive (SOM) and serotonin positive neurons.
evidence: This is a statement of established classification of GABAergic interneurons in the abstract.

claim: In ALM layer five and S1, the PV response is paradoxical: photoexcitation reduces their activity.
source: In ALM layer five and S1, the PV response is paradoxical: photoexcitation reduces their activity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The paradoxical effect does not occur in ALM layer 2/3.
source: This is not the case in ALM layer 2/3.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Two-population models cannot explain the experimental results.
source: Two-population models cannot explain the results.
evidence: This is a conclusion from theoretical modeling stated in the abstract.

claim: Four-population networks with V1-like architecture account for the data in ALM layer 2/3 and layer 5.
source: Four-population networks with V1-like architecture account for the data in ALM layer 2/3 and layer 5.
evidence: This is a conclusion from theoretical modeling stated in the abstract.

claim: Data in S1 can be explained if SOM neurons receive inputs only from PCs and PV neurons.
source: Our data in S1 can be explained if SOM neurons receive inputs only from PCs and PV neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion from theoretical modeling stated in the abstract.

claim: In both four-population models, the paradoxical effect implies not too strong recurrent excitation.
source: In both four-population models, the paradoxical effect implies not too strong recurrent excitation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from theoretical modeling stated in the abstract.

claim: The paradoxical effect is not evidence for stabilization by inhibition.
source: It is not evidence for stabilization by inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion from theoretical modeling stated in the abstract.

claim: Local cortical circuits comprise several subclasses of GABAergic interneurons which together with the excitatory neurons form complex recurrent networks.
source: Local cortical circuits comprise several subclasses of GABAergic interneurons which together with the excitatory neurons form complex recurrent networks (Goldberg et al., 2004; Jiang et al., 2015; Karnani et al., 2016; Markram et al., 2004; Moore et al., 2010; Pfeffer et al., 2013; Tasic et al., 2018; Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The architecture of cortical networks depends on the cortical area and layer.
source: The architecture of these networks depends on the cortical area and layer (Beierlein et al., 2003; Jiang et al., 2013; Rudy et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2013; Xu and Callaway, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Optogenetics is now classically used to reversibly inactivate a particular cortical area or neuronal population to get insights into their functions.
source: Optogenetics is now classically used to reversibly inactivate a particular cortical area or neuronal population to get insights into their functions (Atallah et al., 2012; Guo et al., 2014b; Lee et al., 2012; Li et al., 2015; Svoboda and Li, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Optogenetics has been applied to isolate the different components (e.g. feedforward vs. recurrent) of the net input into cortical neurons.
source: Optogenetics has also been applied to isolate the different components (e.g. feedforward vs. recurrent) of the net input into cortical neurons (Lien and Scanziani, 2018; Lien and Scanziani, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Optogenetics can be used to experimentally probe the architecture of local cortical circuits.
source: It can also be used to experimentally probe the architecture of local cortical circuits (Moore et al., 2018; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Because of the complexity of cortical networks and their nonlinear dynamics, qualitative intuition and simple reasoning are of limited use to interpret the results of optogenetic manipulations.
source: However, because of the complexity of these networks and of their nonlinear dynamics, qualitative intuition and simple reasoning (e.g. 'box-and-arrow' diagrams) are of limited use to interpret the results of these manipulations.
evidence: This is a reasoning statement about the limitations of simple approaches.

claim: 'Paradoxical effect' designates the phenomenon that stimulation of a GABAergic interneuron population not only decreases the average activity of the principal cells (PCs) but also decreases the activity of the stimulated population.
source: 'Paradoxical effect' designates the phenomenon that stimulation of a GABAergic interneuron population not only decreases the average activity of the principal cells (PCs) but also decreases the activity of the stimulated population (Murphy and Miller, 2009; Ozeki et al., 2009; Tsodyks et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Paradoxical effect arises when the stimulation induces a strong activity suppression in the PCs.
source: Intuitively, paradoxical effect arises when the stimulation induces a strong activity suppression in the PCs (Kato et al., 2017; Moore et al., 2018), such that the overall (synaptic+stimulus) excitation to the stimulated population decreases.
evidence: This is an intuitive explanation supported by citations.

claim: In simple two-population models, the paradoxical effect occurs when the network operates in the inhibition stabilized regime.
source: In simple models consisting of only two populations (one excitatory and one inhibitory) these conditions have been mathematically derived. The paradoxical effect occurs when the networks operates in the regime known as inhibition stabilized (inhibition stabilized networks, ISN) in which the total the total recurrent excitation is so strong that inhibition is necessary to prevent a blow up in the activity (Murphy and Miller, 2009; Ozeki et al., 2009; Tsodyks et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a statement about prior theoretical work supported by citations.

claim: Networks with several inhibitory populations have been recently investigated.
source: Networks, with several inhibitory populations have been recently investigated (Garcia Del Molino et al., 2017; Litwin-Kumar et al., 2016; Sadeh et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Previous studies of multi-population networks considered network models with synaptic currents small compared to neuronal rheobase currents.
source: These studies considered network models with synaptic currents small compared to neuronal rheobase currents (Gerstner et al., 2014; Lapicque, 1909).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Interactions in cortex are stronger than what is assumed in previous studies of multi-population networks.
source: However, interactions in cortex are stronger than what is assumed in these studies (Shadlen and Newsome, 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Simple networks with strong interactions comprising one excitatory and one inhibitory population have been studied extensively.
source: Simple networks with strong interactions comprising one excitatory and one inhibitory population have been studied extensively.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: In a broad parameter range not requiring fine-tuning, networks with strong interactions dynamically evolve into a state in which strong excitation is balanced by strong inhibition.
source: In a broad parameter range not requiring fine-tuning, such networks dynamically evolve into a state in which strong excitation is balanced by strong inhibition such that the net input into the neurons is comparable to their rheobases (van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1998; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior theoretical work.

claim: The theory of balanced networks has been developed for a variety of single neuronal models.
source: The theory of balanced networks has been developed for a variety of single neuronal models including binary neurons (van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1998; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1996), rate models (Harish and Hansel, 2015; Kadmon and Sompolinsky, 2015), leaky-integrate-and fire neurons (Hansel and Mato, 2013; Mongillo et al., 2012; Rosenbaum and Doiron, 2014; Roxin et al., 2011; Van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 2005) and conductance-based models (Hansel and van Vreeswijk, 2012; Pattadkal et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior theoretical work.

claim: ReaChR was expressed in PV interneurons to optogenetically drive local inhibition in the barrel cortex (S1) and anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM) of awake mice.
source: We expressed a red-shifted channelrhodopsin (ReaChR) in PV interneurons to optogenetically drive local inhibition in the barrel cortex (S1) and anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM) of awake mice (Hooks et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method with a citation.

claim: Orange light (594 nm) was used to illuminate a large area of ALM or S1 (2 mm diameter), photostimulating a large proportion of PV interneurons.
source: We used orange light (594 nm) to illuminate a large area of ALM or S1 (2 mm diameter), photostimulating a large proportion of PV interneurons (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method with reference to a figure.

claim: Putative PCs and putative PV neurons were identified based on spike width.
source: In both brain areas, putative PCs and putative PV neurons were identified based on spike width (Methods).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method.

claim: Neurons with wide spikes were likely mostly PCs.
source: Neurons with wide spikes were likely mostly PCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on spike width classification.

claim: Units with narrow spikes were fast spiking (FS) neurons and likely expressed parvalbumin.
source: Units with narrow spikes were fast spiking (FS) neurons and likely expressed parvalbumin (Cardin et al., 2009; Guo et al., 2014b; Olsen et al., 2012; Resulaj et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on spike width classification supported by citations.

claim: In all recorded layers and areas, the population average activity of the PCs decreased with the optogenetic drive.
source: We found that in all recorded layers and areas, the population average activity of the PCs decreased with the optogenetic drive (Figure 1B, Figure 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with reference to figures.

claim: In ALM, the PV population exhibited a behavior which depended on the recorded layer.
source: In contrast in ALM, the PV population exhibited a behavior which depended on the recorded layer.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: In ALM layer 2/3, the population average firing rate of PV neurons monotonically increased with the photostimulation intensity.
source: In ALM layer 2/3, the population average firing rate of PV neurons monotonically increased with the photostimulation intensity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: Individual PV neuron responses in ALM layer 2/3 were heterogeneous.
source: However, individual neuron responses were heterogeneous.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: Most PV neurons in ALM layer 2/3 increased their spike rates from baseline with increased photostimulation intensity.
source: Most PV neurons increased their spike rates from baseline with increased photostimulation intensity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: Some PV neurons in ALM layer 2/3 initially decreased their spike rates below baseline for low light intensity.
source: Some PV neurons initially decreased their spike rates below baseline for low light intensity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: In ALM layer 5, the response of the PV population was non-monotonic.
source: In ALM layer 5, the response of the PV population was non-monotonic.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: For low laser intensity in ALM layer 5, PV activity paradoxically decreased with the optogenetic drive.
source: For low laser intensity, their activity paradoxically decreased with the optogenetic drive.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: The slope of the normalized firing rate v.s. laser intensity was significantly different from zero for both the PC and PV populations in ALM layer 5.
source: The slope of the normalized firing rate v.s. laser intensity was significantly different from zero for both the PC and PV populations (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with reference to a figure.

claim: The ratio of the slopes of PC and PV firing rates in ALM layer 5 was 0.62 ± 0.28.
source: The ratio of their slopes was 0.62 ± 0.28.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: At high photostimulation intensity in ALM layer 5, the activity of the PV population increased.
source: At high photostimulation intensity, the activity of the PV population increased.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: At intermediate photostimulation intensity (0.5 mW/mm2), the response of the PV neurons was significantly different between ALM layer 2/3 and layer 5.
source: At intermediate photostimulation intensity (0.5 mW/mm2), the response of the PV neurons was significantly different between layer 2/3 and layer 5 (Figure 1E, p<0.005, unpaired t-test, two-tailed test).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Paradoxical decrease in PV neurons activity with the optogenetic drive was also observed in S1.
source: Paradoxical decrease in PV neurons activity with the optogenetic drive was also observed in S1.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: In S1, the concomitant decrease of the PC and the PV population activities was proportional.
source: Remarkably, the concomitant decrease of the PC and the PV population activities was proportional (Figure 1G, ratio of slopes PV/PC, mean ± SEM; S1, 1 ± 0.29).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: In both ALM layer 5 and S1, there was a large diversity of responses.
source: In both ALM layer 5 and S1, there was also a large diversity of responses.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: Most PV neurons in ALM layer 5 and S1 decreased their activity at low photostimulation intensity.
source: Most PV neurons decreased their activity at low photostimulation intensity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: At high laser intensity (5 mW/mm2), a fraction of PV neurons (6/12 in ALM layer 5 and 6/10 in S1) had a larger response than baseline, while the rest remained suppressed.
source: At high laser intensity (5 mW/mm2), a fraction of PV neurons (6/12 in ALM layer 5 and 6/10 in S1) had a larger response than baseline, while the rest remained suppressed.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: The laser diameter was substantially larger than the spatial range of neuronal interactions and comparable to the size of the area in which activity was recorded.
source: The data we seek to account for, were obtained in optogenetic experiments in which the laser diameter was substantially larger than the spatial range of neuronal interactions and comparable to the size of the area in which activity was recorded.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental conditions.

claim: In all models, the connectivity is assumed to be unstructured.
source: Therefore, in all our models, we assume for simplicity that the connectivity is unstructured.
evidence: This is a modeling assumption.

claim: Two-population network models do not fully account for the experimental data.
source: We showed that two-population network models of strongly interacting neurons do not fully account for the experimental data.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work.

claim: In the two-population model, the minimum of the PV activity is reached when excitatory neurons are virtually completely silenced.
source: This is because the mechanism requires strong recurrent excitation. In the four-population networks we studied, however, the mechanism responsible for paradoxical effect is different. It involves a disinhibitory loop. In fact, strong recurrent excitation prevents the paradoxical effect in these networks.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work with reference to an appendix.

claim: In the two-population model, proportional decrease of PC and PV activities only happens when the determinant of the interaction matrix is close to zero.
source: Analytical calculations (Appendix 1B) supplemented with numerical simulations show that this proportional decrease only happens when the determinant of the interaction matrix, J αβ, is close to zero.

claim: The two-population model can account for the ALM layer 2/3 data only if the recurrent excitation is very weak and the connectivity is extremely sparse.
source: In Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, we show that the two-population model can account for this feature only if the recurrent excitation is very weak in that layer and the connectivity is extremely sparse.

claim: Model 1 consists of four populations representing PCs, PV, SOM and VIP neurons.
source: The model consists of four populations representing PCs, PV, SOM and VIP neurons.

claim: In Model 1, SOM neurons do not interact with each other.
source: SOM neurons do not interact with each other (Adesnik et al., 2012; Gibson et al., 1999; Hu et al., 2011).

claim: In Model 1, VIP neurons only project to the SOM population.
source: VIP neurons only project to the SOM population (Jiang et al., 2015; Pfeffer et al., 2013).

claim: In Model 1, all neurons except SOM receive inputs from sources external to the network.
source: All neurons except SOM receive inputs from sources external to the network (e.g. thalamus) (Beierlein et al., 2003; Beierlein et al., 2000; Cruikshank et al., 2010; Ma et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2013).

claim: The architecture of Model 1 was considered in Litwin-Kumar et al. (2016).
source: The same architecture was considered in Litwin-Kumar et al. (2016).

source: When ρ > 1, the PV response is non-paradoxical and its activity increase can be substantial well before suppression of the PC activity.

source: On the other hand when ρ > 1, the PV response is paradoxical and the PV activity reaches its minimum for light intensities at which the PCs are still substantially active.

claim: Model 1 accounts for experimental findings in ALM layer 2/3 provided that J_EE is sufficiently large.
source: Thus, Model 1 accounts for our experimental findings in ALM layer 2/3 provided that JEE is sufficiently large.

source: It accounts for the paradoxical effect in layer 5 provided that JEE is sufficiently small.

claim: In Model 2, the co-modulation of the PC and PV activities stems from the architecture and therefore occurs in a robust manner.

source: The main difference between Models 1 and 2 is that in Model 1, the third inhibitory population (VIP) projects to SOM neurons while in Model 2, the third population (X) does not.

source: For example, X could be chandelier cells that do not express the PV marker (Jiang et al., 2015)

claim: Population X in Model 2 could describe the effective interaction of several inhibitory populations with PC and PV neurons.
source: Alternatively, population X could describe the effective interaction of several inhibitory populations with PC and PV neurons.

claim: The responses of PCs and PV neurons in the experimental data are highly heterogeneous across cells.
source: The responses of PCs and PV neurons in the experimental data are highly heterogeneous across cells.

claim: The firing rate of a neuron can vary monotonically or non-monotonically with the laser intensity.

claim: In the present study with static synapses, changes in the background rates cannot reverse the paradoxical effect.
source: Since we used static synapses, changes in the background rates cannot reverse the paradoxical effect in our models.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work.

claim: With static synapses, the balance equations are linear.
source: This is because with static synapses the balance equations are linear.
evidence: This is a statement about the mathematical properties of the model.

claim: One can recover the reversal of the paradoxical effect if one introduces short-term plasticity which will make the balance equations nonlinear.
source: One can recover this reversal if one introduces short-term plasticity which will make the balance equations nonlinear.
evidence: This is a speculation about extending the model.

claim: Partial expression of channelrhodopsin in the PV population was not considered because the goal was to account for experimental data where virtually all neurons were infected.
source: We did not consider partial expression of channelrhodopsin in the PV population because our goal was to account for experimental data where virtually all neurons were infected.
evidence: This is a description of a modeling choice.

claim: Effects of partial expression have been studied in Gutnisky et al. (2017); Sanzeni et al. (2019) in strongly coupled networks of two populations yielding to the same conclusions as Sadeh et al. (2017).
source: These effects have been studied in Gutnisky et al. (2017); Sanzeni et al. (2019) in strongly coupled networks of two populations yielding to the same conclusions as (Sadeh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about prior work supported by citations.

claim: The theory (Model 1) predicts that in ALM layer 2/3 the activity of the SOM and VIP populations will decrease upon PV photostimulation.
source: Our theory (Model 1) predicts that in ALM layer 2/3 the activity of the SOM and VIP populations will decrease upon PV photostimulation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to a figure.

claim: The theory (Model 1) predicts that upon PC photoinhibition in ALM layer 2/3, the PV activity will increase whereas the activity of the SOM and VIP populations will decrease.
source: It also predicts that upon PC photoinhibition, the PV activity will increase whereas the activity of the SOM and VIP populations will decrease (Figure 12A).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to a figure.

claim: In ALM layer 2/3 the population activity of PCs decreases upon PV photostimulation, so χ_EI < 0.
source: Furthermore, in ALM layer 2/3 the population activity of PCs decreases upon PV photostimulation, XEI < 0.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental data.

claim: In ALM layer 2/3, χ_IE is negative.
source: Hence, XIE is negative.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work.

claim: The balance of the PC and the VIP inputs into SOM neurons implies that VIP and PC activity covary.
source: The balance of the PC and the VIP inputs into SOM neurons implies that VIP and PC activity covary.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work.

claim: If χ_EE > 0 and χ_IE < 0 then necessarily χ_SE > 0.
source: Finally, in Appendix 1C we show that if XEE  > 0 and XIE < 0 then necessarily XSE > 0.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work with reference to an appendix.

claim: In ALM layer 2/3, the SOM population activity should decrease upon PC photoinhibition.
source: Thus, in ALM layer 2/3, the SOM population activity should decrease upon PC photoinhibition (Figure 12A).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to a figure.

claim: In auditory and prefrontal cortex as well as in S1, photostimulation of VIP neurons, activates them (χ_VV > 0) and disinhibits the PCs (χ_EV > 0) through an inhibition of the SOM population (χ_SV > 0).
source: In auditory and prefrontal cortex (Pi et al., 2013) as well as in S1 (Lee et al., 2013), photostimulation of VIP neurons, activates them (XVV > 0) and disinhibits the PCs (XEV > 0) through an inhibition of the SOM population (XSV > 0).
evidence: This is a statement about prior experimental work supported by citations.

claim: If VIP photostimulation activates VIP neurons and disinhibits PCs in ALM layer 2/3, the model predicts that photostimulation of VIP neurons should increase the PV activity (χ_IV > 0).
source: If this is also true in ALM layer 2/3, our model predicts that photostimulation of VIP neurons should increase the PV activity (XIV > 0) (Appendix 1C, Figure 12B).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to an appendix and a figure.

claim: The theory (Model 2) predicts that the PC and PV activities will proportionally decrease upon PC photoinhibition in S1.
source: In S1 our theory (Model 2) predicts that the PC and PV activities will proportionally decrease upon PC photoinhibition (Equation (3), Appendix 1D, Figure 12C).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to an equation, appendix, and figure.

claim: Photostimulation of the SOM neurons modifies Equation (3) and consequently, the changes in PC and PV activity no longer covary.
source: Photostimulation of the SOM neurons modifies Equation (3) and consequently, the changes in PC and PV activity no longer covary (Figure 12D).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to a figure.

claim: The theory can be tested by photostimulating PV neurons while also photostimulating SOM neurons with a second laser with constant power.
source: Thus, our theory can be tested by photostimulating PV neurons as in our experiment, while also photostimulating SOM neurons with a second laser with constant power.
evidence: This is a proposed experimental test of the model.

claim: In the proposed experiment, the model predicts that S1 will still exhibit the paradoxical effect but that the responses of the PC and PV populations will no longer be proportional.
source: In this case, the model predicts that S1 will still exhibit the paradoxical effect but that the responses of the PC and PV populations will no longer be proportional (Figure 12E).
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling work with reference to a figure.

claim: The theory can be extended to incorporate spatial dependencies.
source: Our theory can be extended to incorporate spatial dependencies.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: Studying the interplay between the connectivity pattern and laser beam width in the response profile of the networks will provide further constraints on cortical architectures.
source: Studying the interplay between the connectivity pattern and laser beam width in the response profile of the networks will provide further constraints on cortical architectures.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: Due to the strong interactions in the models, the nonlinearity of the single neuron f-I curves hardly affects the population average responses.
source: Due to the strong interactions in our models, the nonlinearity of the single neuron f-I curves hardly affects the population average responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work.

claim: The nonlinearity of the single neuron f-I curves influences the response heterogeneity that naturally arises in the theory.
source: However, it influences the response heterogeneity that naturally arises in our theory (Figures 6–8).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work with reference to figures.

claim: An alternative model for the paradoxical effect is the supralinear stabilized network (SSN) which relies on an expansive non-linearity of the input-output transfer function of the inhibitory populations.
source: An alternative model for the paradoxical effect is the supralinear stabilized network (SSN) (Rubin et al., 2015) which relies on an expansive non-linearity of the input-output transfer function of the inhibitory populations.
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative model supported by a citation.

claim: Whether the SSN scenario can account for the experimental data is an issue for further study.
source: Whether this mechanism can account for our experimental data is an issue for further study.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: It would be interesting to know whether the SSN scenario can account for the strong heterogeneity in the responses and for the proportionality of the PC and PV population activities in S1.
source: In particular, it would be interesting to know whether the SSN scenario can account for the strong heterogeneity in the responses and for the proportionality of the PC and PV population activities in S1.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: Answering questions about the SSN scenario may provide a way to discriminate between the balance network and SSN theory.
source: Answering these questions may provide a way to discriminate between the balance network and SSN theory.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: The experimental data are from 9 PV-Ires-Cre x R26-CAG-LSL-ReaChR-mCitrine mice (age >P60, both male and female mice).
source: The experimental data are from 9 PV-Ires-Cre x R26-CAG-LSL-ReaChR-mCitrine mice (age >P60, both male and female mice) (Hooks et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects with a citation.

claim: Three mice were used for photoinhibition in somatosensory cortex (S1).
source: three mice were used for photoinhibition in somatosensory cortex (S1).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects.

claim: Six mice were used for photoinhibition in anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM).
source: six mice were used for photoinhibition in anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects.
